---
title: "SciGraphs panels"
---

::: {.lead}
Seven walkthroughs of the **SciGraphs** tab, one per panel, each following a
concrete case so you can reproduce the result button by button.
:::

These are the worked "typical workflows" referenced from the
[Panel Reference](../../../panels/overview.qmd). Unlike the OSMnx and City2Graph
sets, this one is not about real-world geography: the SciGraphs tab works on any
graph, and its job is to give that graph positions, measurements, an appearance
and a reproducible record.

## The tutorials

| # | Tutorial | Panel | After it you can |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | [Load a graph](data.qmd) | [Data](../../../panels/scigraphs/data.qmd) | Import a graph from a file, a SQL database, SuiteSparse or a pipeline, and build the Blender object every other panel operates on. |
| 2 | [Lay it out](layout.qmd) | [Layout & Positioning](../../../panels/scigraphs/layout.qmd) | Give a graph with no coordinates a set of positions, in 2D or 3D, and pick an algorithm that finishes on the size you have. |
| 3 | [Run algorithms](algorithms.qmd) | [Graph Algorithms](../../../panels/scigraphs/algorithms.qmd) | Traverse the graph, find shortest paths, build spanning trees, solve flows, and animate the result. |
| 4 | [Measure the network](analysis.qmd) | [Analysis](../../../panels/scigraphs/analysis.qmd) | Compute centralities, detect communities and read global statistics, each stored as a mesh attribute you can encode visually. |
| 5 | [Make it look right](visualization.qmd) | [Visualization](../../../panels/scigraphs/visualization.qmd) | Turn those attributes into node and edge geometry, color, materials, lighting and on-render labels. |
| 6 | [Get it back out](export.qmd) | [Export & Tools](../../../panels/scigraphs/export.qmd) | Write the graph to a standard format, export node positions, and generate a statistics report. |
| 7 | [Freeze and replay it](reproducibility.qmd) | [Reproducibility](../../../panels/scigraphs/reproducibility.qmd) | Capture the whole workflow in one JSON or YAML file, replay it deterministically, and audit the provenance manifest it writes. |

::: {.callout-tip}
New to the add-on? Enable SciGraphs (see
[Installation](../../../guide/installation.qmd)), open the 3D Viewport sidebar
with `N`, pick the **SciGraphs** tab, and start with [Load a graph](data.qmd).
:::

## The same ground from a console

The [Jupyter notebooks](../../../notebooks/index.qmd) run inside Blender and
cover this tab with the timings, distributions and failure modes measured rather
than described. The tutorials show you where the buttons are; the notebooks show
you what the numbers do.

| Notebook | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| [01 Abstract graphs](../../../notebooks/01-abstract-graphs.qmd) | Importing and building graphs that carry no coordinates. |
| [02 Layouts](../../../notebooks/02-layouts.qmd) | The layout algorithms, and what each one costs. |
| [03 Centrality and communities](../../../notebooks/03-centrality-communities.qmd) | Centrality measures and community detection. |
| [04 Paths, trees and flows](../../../notebooks/04-paths-trees-flows.qmd) | Traversal, shortest paths, spanning trees, network flow. |
| [05 Topology](../../../notebooks/05-topology.qmd) | Topological invariants and structural analysis. |

For scripting the add-on rather than clicking it, see the
[Python API reference](../../../reference/python-api.qmd).

## Where the other tabs fit

A street network downloaded in the [OSMnx panels](../osmnx/download.qmd) or an
urban graph built in the [City2Graph panels](../city2graph/data.qmd) arrives as
an ordinary SciGraphs graph object, and everything from panel 3 onwards applies
to it unchanged. The exception is [Layout](layout.qmd): geographic data already
has positions, so that panel is for graphs that have none.
